$comment: The local IPC contract between the Mesh desktop application and the Mesh daemon, published by the daemon because the daemon owns the surface (task 01KZC2NJ6WEZ0ZHP6Z03FJGVF3, `## Scope`). ONE file, read by both implementations, so that neither can drift without a test going red: `crates/mesh-daemon/tests/ipc.rs` checks the Rust side against it and `apps/desktop/src/ipc/contract.test.ts` checks the TypeScript side. `vectors` are exact wire lines: each side decodes one, re-encodes it, and compares BYTE FOR BYTE. That is what makes `deterministic encoding` a measurement rather than a claim. This is NOT the canonical signed encoding of plan §4 — that is CBOR and it lives in `mesh-types`. Nothing on this socket is signed.

framing.note: Each line remains bounded. Surface 7 splits a larger canonical daemon message into ordered lower-case-hex chunk frames and reconstructs at most max_message_bytes; older clients receive a small response-too-large failure.

transport.note: The daemon binds a filesystem path and never a network address; the desktop client connects to a filesystem path and never opens a listener of any kind. Both claims are tested: `crates/mesh-daemon/tests/ipc.rs` and `apps/desktop/src/ipc/no-network.test.ts`.

compatibility.additive_within_a_version: An ANSWER may gain keys inside a surface version, and a client ignores what it does not recognise. Removing a key, renaming one, or changing what an existing key means is NOT additive and needs a new surface version. `workspace.state` gained `private_version` that way: the method catalogue did not move, `supported_versions` did not move, and a version 1 client still cannot reach the method at all.
compatibility.note: Stated here rather than in a commit message, because the reader who needs it is a client author outside this repository.

private_version.note: `version` is this replica's own version identifier, derived by mesh-state over the saved changes actually on disk, using each record's own causal parents; it is null when there are no saved changes and therefore no head. It is NOT checked against what the authors claimed: a ChangeSet carries a base and a resulting version, the saved record persists neither, so there is no claim on disk to disagree with. `state` is the review-axis word - working, ready for review, superseded or archived. `waiting` reports every waiting change and every absent parent, while `waiting_not_listed` remains zero as a compatibility field. `apply_order_agrees` reports whether mesh-state and mesh-materializer, two independent implementations of causal depth then identifier, produced the same order over the same complete on-disk record set.

shared_version.derivation: ordered durable HumanHeld publication decisions plus canonical approval receipts
shared_version.note: The value remains null and `not_yet` retains the shared-version refusal until the immutable journal can carry mesh-policy's recorded HumanHeld publication authority beside the exact signed receipt. A configured public key or a software-held signature alone never advances it.

file_histories.derivation: complete materialized state reconstructed from verified immutable operation payloads
file_histories.note: Each row binds a currently materialized file path and stable object identifier to every retained immutable version and manifest identifier. It is read-only discovery for `workspace.restore.preview`, not restore authority. An incomplete materialization returns no history and reports the recoverable conditions instead of exposing a plausible partial list.

workspace_versions.derivation: causally complete durable operation points in deterministic causal order
workspace_versions.note: Each row is a read-only operation identity that can be supplied to workspace.version.fork. A fork reconstructs only that operation and its transitive parents, verifies every manifest and chunk, and creates a new independent private store plus ordinary mounts working folder. It never rewinds or mutates the source workspace.

native_untracked_files.derivation: metadata-only enumeration of regular files in the presented native folder minus complete durable materialization paths
native_untracked_files.note: This additive list is nonauthoritative discovery for local clients. It never follows symlinks, reads file contents, creates an operation, or claims that a short-lived or unreadable file is absent. A client must use the native inspect-and-adopt path, bound to the exact workspace installation and content digest, before representing a listed file as saved.

native_unsupported_entries.derivation: metadata-only classification of included symbolic links, special objects, and re-included paths below excluded parents in the presented native folder
native_unsupported_entries.note: This additive list makes unsupported native content visible without following or reading it. Each row has a root-relative path and the closed kind symbolic-link, special, or excluded-ancestor. The exact app-owned .codex navigation link is excluded only when its target, private directory permissions, and one-file generated configuration shape all match. An excluded-ancestor row requires the person to include its parent too or keep the descendant excluded. Clients must block complete-save and review claims until every listed entry is made representable, excluded by an explicit rule, or removed.

native_inventory_complete.derivation: whether the metadata-only native inventory read and classified every directory entry it encountered
native_inventory_complete.note: False is a fail-closed signal: the response may still carry paths Mesh did observe, but a client must not claim the workspace is completely scanned or allow review and approval until a fresh inventory completes. Older clients may ignore this additive key; this desktop treats an absent key from an older daemon as its prior compatibility behavior.

support_bundle.derivation: the running daemon's already-verified journal boundary and restored checkpoint snapshot
support_bundle.note: This additive answer is the same allowlisted mesh-support-bundle/v1 document available from the endpoint-free inspector, but it consumes the open daemon's coherent in-memory truth so an ordinary live SQLite WAL family is not mislabeled as crash damage. Clients must bind the returned root to the workspace they intended before displaying the document.

performance.counters.conditions: a load-dependent reading is wall-clock nanoseconds and moves with machine load; the conditions a timing number is taken under are benchmarks/runners/README.md, `Getting a trustworthy number`

not_yet_reason_groups.reason: this build assembles no agent context, so nothing here is ever observed in it
the filesystem operation exists, but no operation-level metric producer is wired in this build
the read is not timed apart from the fold that follows it; the whole open is recorded on workspace_operations.index_reconstruction.ns
no build or test runs inside a Mesh workspace are measured here
no process accounting is read on any platform in this build
this build opens no network transport, so nothing here is ever observed in it
the operation exists, but no workspace-operation metric producer is wired in this build

performance.counters.consistency: Related product counters remain under one writer bracket, and the client independently re-derives the saturating observation sum and snapshot_consistent verdict from the published readings; the daemon flag is not trusted by itself.

push.note: The one line the daemon sends that no client message asked for, and it is sent only to a connection that called `events.subscribe`. Its `id` is that call's identifier, so a client correlates a push with the request that opened the stream. `sequence` orders entries ON THIS SOCKET and nothing else: ordering of work in Mesh is `lamport -> event id -> content hash`, and a feed sequence establishes none of those. A client that never subscribes never receives one, which is what makes version 2 additive.
